notes: Step 1 parts were correct; no parts added or dropped.
Circuit: pushbutton between Arduino pin 2 and GND, no external resistor (internal INPUT_PULLUP is used).

In the image the breadboard is drawn with rows numbered 1-30 down the side and letters A-J across. Following the catalogue naming, row 24 left half is strip '24t' (A-E) and right half is '24b' (F-J). Row 25 works the same way.
The black wire goes from the Arduino GND header pin (next to AREF) to row 24, hole A. The yellow wire goes from digital pin 2 to row 25, hole A.

The button straddles the centre gap with legs at E24, F24, E25 and F25. Side 1 (1.l/1.r) sits in row 24, which is GND. Side 2 (2.l/2.r) sits in row 25, which is pin 2. Pressing the button joins pin 2 to GND.
GND.1 is assumed to be the GND pin on the digital header next to AREF, as drawn in the image.
The tutorial's code also drives the on-board LED on pin 13. This is built into the board, so no external LED or resistor is added.
